name: Executed commands
description: Every command the build executed, read from the session a running `buildnote monitor` records on the runner. This is what the job actually ran, not what a pipeline file says it would run.

sessionsDir.description: Directory holding the monitor sessions. When unset, the collector reads the CLI's own `BUILDNOTE_MONITOR_DIR`, which is where `buildnote monitor` records and which the CLI resolves so this collector does not have to guess. If you run the collector by hand with neither set, it falls back to `buildnote-monitor` under the temporary directory.

maxExecutions.description: How many executions to report before the rest are left out and counted in `dropped`. The earliest are kept, so a command run near the start of the job is still reported when the build goes past the limit later on.

facts.source: `report` when a monitor session was read, `none` when there was none.
facts.reason: Why there was none, present only when `source` is `none`.
facts.reports[].path: Absolute path of the session file on the runner. A monitor records outside the checkout, so this is the one path in the facts that is not stated from the directory the CLI runs in.
facts.reports[].modified: When it was last written, ISO 8601. A session still being appended to was written seconds ago.
facts.monitor: The monitor whose session was read.
facts.monitor.running: Whether the monitor is still recording, meaning the session has no closing record. `false` means the monitor finished and the commands are the whole of what it traced.
facts.monitor.matched: How the session was chosen: `build` when it records the build this run belongs to, which is the case whenever the monitor and the guardrails run in the same job, and `recent` when no session names this build and the most recent one was read instead.
facts.monitor.sessions: How many sessions were found in that directory. More than one means another monitor has recorded on this runner.
facts.monitor.pid: Process the monitor is running as.
facts.monitor.startedAt: When the monitor started recording, epoch milliseconds.
facts.monitor.closedAt: When it stopped, epoch milliseconds, or `null` while it is still recording.
facts.monitor.build: Build the monitor recorded for, which is what `matched` compares against.
facts.monitor.module: Module the monitor submits its commands under.
facts.monitor.command: The command the monitor launched, or `null` when it attached to a process it did not start.
facts.commands: Every command that was executed, one entry per execution, in the order they were executed. A command run twice is two entries.
facts.commands[].command: The command line, exactly as the process was executed, truncated to 2000 characters. Arguments are separated by single spaces and their original quoting is gone: this is the process's argument vector joined, not the shell line that produced it.
facts.commands[].pid: Process the command ran as. A pid is reused within a job, so it identifies an execution only alongside its timestamp.
facts.commands[].startedAt: When it was executed, epoch milliseconds.
facts.commands[].durationMs: How long it ran, milliseconds, or `null` when it was not seen to exit.
facts.commands[].exitCode: The code it exited with, or `null` when it was not seen to exit, which is a command still running or one the monitor stopped tracing before it finished.
facts.counts.executions: How many commands were executed in total, including any left out by `maxExecutions`.
facts.counts.commands: How many distinct command lines are among the executions reported.
facts.dropped: Executions left out because `maxExecutions` was reached. Above zero, the list describes only part of the build: a command found here is real, but a command missing from it is not proof the build never ran it, so a check that would otherwise report clean must skip.
